newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares rebound early, Nippecraft sinks.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares rebound early, Nippecraft sinks.

text.p: Singapore blue chip shares were firmer early on Friday, but shares in stationery-maker Nippecraft resumed trading weaker after a major stockholder sold its holding.

"Nippecraft will take some time to stablise and could head lower based on the sale price (per share) of its stock," a dealer with a local brokerage said. The company said the shareholder sold its 64 percent stake for $0.035 cents a share.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose 11.41 points to 2,202.04 on a brisk turnover of 107 million shares at 0130 GMT.
Dealers said the rebound was not strong, but selective buying of blue chips was helping to lift the index.
Malaysian over-the-counter stocks also recovered from a sharp fall late Thursday, but dealers said sentiment was cautious with profit taking continuing to limit the upside.
Net gainers included SPH foreign, up Singapore $0.50 at S$27.80, OCBC foreign, up S$0.50 to $19.20 and Creative Technology, up S$0.40 at $18.60.
Nippecraft shed 9.7 percent of its share price to S$0.60, down six cents, and Malaysia's Public Bank succumbed to profit taking, down six cents to S$3.32.
